chapter: Reel 1: childhood, first songs, Fats Waller
title: What Fats Waller was like and how publishers loved him
summary: Fats filled a room, sold the same song to six publishers and no one got angry, and everyone on Broadway loved him.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: And he knew it when he saw it. Now, when you first met him, and he was 19 -- what was he like? What was he like?
Just a youngster full of vim, vigor and wigor! Just full of everything that you have at 19 years old!
And he was full of it, and big enough to have a lot of it.
So, oh, golly -- when Fats came in, everybody had to move over, because the room got smaller.

So he was the most wonderful guy -- I don't know of anyone in my life that publishes on Broadway would do what they did with Fats. Fats would sell the same songs to six publishers, and not one of those publishers would ever get angry with Fats.
You just couldn't. He was under your skin and he stayed there. He lived under your skin.
Oh, that's a nice way to put it.
That's right, and he was just so wonderful because you would ask Fats for a song one day, maybe two weeks later, he'd say, 'Take it, take it.' They all got
paid for what they did. They enjoyed it and they loved him, they loved him -- I never saw a guy yet who held a spot that he held in the hearts of those tough guys down Broadway. But he was one.
Uh huh. And you held the spot in his heart.
